content: Stress corrosion cracking was responsible for numerous structural failures across the United States during the 1980s and 1990s. One notable instance involved an acetal joint within a water supply system. When this joint fractured, it led to significant physical damage to computers located in laboratories situated beneath the water supply system. The origin of the cracks was traced to defects formed during the injection molding process of the joint. These cracks propagated gradually over time until they ultimately caused the joint to fail.
